## Status of the record

The earlier part of this session is not in my context now. I cannot report those findings from memory. So I read both files again. What follows is a fresh read, not a recall.

Files: `fixture/rotate_logs.py` and `fixture/tests/test_rotate_logs.py`.

## Confirmed: `compress()` destroys an existing archive

`compress()` builds the target name at `fixture/rotate_logs.py:20`. It opens that target with mode `"wb"` at line 21. This mode truncates a `.gz` file that already exists. Line 23 then deletes the source file. The old archive content is gone. The run prints a success count and reports no error.

Failure path:

1. A run compresses `a.log` into `a.log.gz`.
2. The log writer creates a new `a.log`.
3. The new `a.log` ages past `--days`.
4. The next run overwrites `a.log.gz`. The first archive is lost.

A fixed log filename makes this the normal case, not a rare one.

## Confirmed: no test covers the collision

The test file holds three tests:

- `test_compresses_old_logs` — one old log, one new log.
- `test_dry_run_touches_nothing` — dry run only.
- `test_prunes_to_keep` — five logs with distinct names.

No test creates a `.gz` file before it calls `rotate()`. Every log name in the tests is unique. So the overwrite case has zero coverage.

## Also found in this read (new, not part of the earlier work)

- `prune_archives()` deletes nothing when `keep` is `0`. The slice `archives[:-0]` at line 29 is empty, not the whole list. `--keep 0` should remove all archives. It removes none.
- `prune_archives()` globs `*.gz` across the whole directory at line 28. It ignores `--pattern`. A run with `--pattern app*.log` can delete `db.log.gz`, which that run did not create.

I did not verify these two by execution. I read them from the code only.

## What I recommend next

1. Decide the wanted behavior on a name collision. The two candidates are a unique target name (a counter or an mtime stamp) and a hard refusal that keeps the source file.
2. Fix `compress()` to match that decision. Keep the source file until the write succeeds.
3. Add a regression test that writes `a.log.gz` first, then rotates a new `a.log`.
4. Fix the `keep=0` slice, or reject `--keep 0` at the argument parser.
5. Decide whether `prune_archives()` must respect `--pattern`.

Items 1 through 3 are the data-loss path. Items 4 and 5 are separate calls and can wait.

Tell me which option you want for item 1. I will then write the fix and the test.
